text:
alex: Quick sync — trying to land a design for packing-aware headroom and a routing-driven admission API for Dedicated pools. TL;DR: want predictable tail latency for latency-tier tenants while keeping unit cost reasonable. thoughts?

maya: curious — what's the core tension you're seeing?

alex: two things: (1) when we pack many small tenant slots onto multi-GPU nodes (MIG / fractional) we get high utilization but noisy tail latencies when eviction/evaporation happens; (2) routing currently just rounds-robin compatible variants and doesn't convey admission pressure back to the orchestrator.

sam: could we encode a per-route backpressure token in the request header? then the orch can throttle by route priority.

lee: important: admission signals mustn't leak PII. token can be an opaque integer + priority enum. orch-bot: note — also consider attack surface (flooding tokens).

alex: agreed. proposal idea: "packing-aware headroom" = per-shard headroom budget expressed in GPUs (or fractional units) + a fastpath for latency SLO tenants that consumes from a reserved soft-reserve pool. non-latency tenants use elastic reservoir.

maya: how do we account warmup costs? prewarm vs on-demand matters for cost.

alex: plan: two credit types — warmup credits and burst credits. warmup credits pay for prewarmed KV cache and model weights pinned to node. burst credits let a tenant exceed steady capacity for N seconds and then decay. credits charged to the tenant's quota.

sam: sounds reasonable. what about packing / fragmentation? if a node has 2x 25%free slots across GPUs, we should avoid leaving them stranded.

lee: packing heuristic: admission API includes a "packing hint" that allows schedulers to binpack cross-GPU if tenant allows multi-slice allocation. otherwise prefer single-GPU contiguous allocation.

alex: exact proto (PSEUDO):
```
POST /v1/admit
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "route": "text-gen-low-latency",
  "priority": "p0",
  "burst_token": 3,
  "packing_hint": "binpack-allowed",
  "max_latency_ms": 120
}
```
returns 200 + {"admit": true, "lease": "lease-xyz", "warmup": "node-5"} or 429 + backoff.

maya: eviction semantics? soft-preempt vs hard-kill?

alex: soft-preempt: send graceful drain signal with TTL (e.g., 10s) and admit fallback model variant. Operator initiates reclaim only after TTL. Hard-kill only for infra emergencies.

sam: how do we ensure fairness during sustained bursts? elastic reservoir could be gamed.

alex: we add amortized leak-rate: every tenant has a refill-rate proportional to paid tier; burst draws down bucket then replenishes slowly. also add global cost-band caps to stop tail risk.

lee: telemetry needs: per-tenant admitted rate, warmup time histogram, slot fragmentation metric, node packing saturation, epoch-level eviction counts. we should tag traces with admit_reason.

maya: ops question: rollout plan? I want a gradual gate with canary tenants and dry-run where routing gets admit:false counts but still forwards.

alex: rollout steps: (1) implement admit API and local scheduler hooks behind flag, (2) enable routing to emit backpressure header, dry-run for 2 weeks, (3) enable soft-reserve pool for p0 tenants (canary group), (4) enable amortized billing, (5) full launch.

sam: minor: add a fast fallback path in the runtime to swap to a smaller-quantized variant if admission fails — reduces user-facing 429s.

lee: security: make sure admit decisions are auditable and signed in control plane, include reason codes for any 429.

alex: open questions: how big should soft-reserve be (percent of cluster), and do we expose credit rules to customers as explicit config or keep as server-side defaults?

maya: prefer defaults with feature flags. exposing config invites complicated SLAs. but allow enterprise tenants to opt-in to explicit soft-reserve buys.

sam: agree. propose default soft-reserve = 8% of Dedicated pool capacity, enterprise can buy bump to 20% with SLA.

lee: quick engineering ask: we need an operator-level reconciliation job to detect stranded fragments and emit compaction hints. add to backlog.

alex: next steps — I'll draft a short RFC with: admit API proto, credit accounting, packing hints, eviction lifecycle, telemetry, and rollout plan. @maya @sam @lee please review the draft when I post. :thumbsup:

orch-bot: deployed checklist created: rfc-draft-1759109876 -> reviewers [maya,sam,lee] -> due 3d

maya: thanks, looking forward to the RFC. :fire:
